corrections: db-choosing-q6: The previously selected architecture fails the stated ordering, latency and partition-availability combination.
db-choosing-q8: A database marker cannot atomically deduplicate a nontransactional external email send.
db-partitioning-q11: Doubling a modulo shard count moves half of uniformly hashed keys, not almost all.
db-relational-acid-q1: Physical WAL recovery is not restricted to committed transactions.
db-storage-internals-q2: Removed unsupported universal compaction amplification range and incorrect worst-case inference.
db-storage-internals-q11: Non-overlap per level bounds point lookups, not the number of files intersecting a range.
db-indexing-q2: Leftmost-prefix rule was overstated; PG18 skip scan is a documented exception.
db-indexing-q5: Zero scan counts alone do not prove an index safe to remove.
db-indexing-q7: HOT eligibility has a summarizing-index exception.
db-indexing-q8: Sequential InnoDB inserts do not guarantee completely full pages.
db-nosql-families-q1: DynamoDB TTL is asynchronous deletion, not immediate session expiration.
db-nosql-families-q5: Tag-cardinality guidance depends on InfluxDB generation; avoid universal capacity claims.
db-nosql-families-q8: Caching cannot silently preserve strongly consistent reads; eventual mode alone still exceeds the item ceiling.
db-storage-internals-q4: Bloom false positives imply possible candidate probes, not guaranteed disk I/O.
db-storage-internals-q5: Removed unsupported universal speedup and equal-column-width inference.
db-storage-internals-q6: Space-amplification percentages were incorrectly presented as universal bounds.
db-storage-internals-q8: ZFS name alone does not establish safe full_page_writes=off; image size may be compressed.
db-storage-internals-q9: Converted unsupported universal performance comparison into an explicitly conditional arithmetic example.
db-transactions-isolation-q5: MVCC does not eliminate table locks; an idle BEGIN alone does not necessarily hold a vacuum horizon.
db-transactions-isolation-q6: Strict 2PL holds exclusive locks; holding every lock is the stronger rigorous form.
db-transactions-isolation-q7: Retry example silently exhausted all retries; external effects need durable handoff.
db-transactions-isolation-q8: Read-only MVCC queries still block some DDL and retain cleanup horizons.
db-transactions-isolation-q9: InnoDB detects/serializes write conflicts with locks; the missing feature is this snapshot-change abort.
db-transactions-isolation-q11: InnoDB detects/serializes write conflicts with locks; the missing feature is this snapshot-change abort.
db-partitioning-q4: Percentile-product arithmetic requires independence and does not determine an exact combined p99.
db-partitioning-q6: Logical salts are not physical partitions; batching requests does not remove byte-based write charges.
db-partitioning-q7: Modulo doubling does not move excess keys; cutover pauses must be explicit and uncoordinated dual writes are unsafe.
db-relational-acid-q8: Normal forms consider every candidate key, not merely the selected primary key.
db-relational-acid-q10: FK alone permits NULL; SQL-standard assertions and schema redesign make universal impossibility wrong.
db-choosing-q1: Removed unsupported PostgreSQL capacity percentage and clarified MongoDB multi-document transaction support.
db-choosing-q2: CDC/outbox guarantees require retention, delivery and error recovery rather than mere architecture.
db-choosing-q3: Removed any-scale claim and unsupported universal warehouse speedup.
db-choosing-q4: CPU utilization does not by itself establish a 4× capacity guarantee.
db-choosing-q7: Removed unsupported current-price savings multiplier and corrected GSI write-cost scope.
db-choosing-q10: On-demand does not eliminate capacity limits or spike planning.
db-choosing-q11: Removed universal single-node limit and unsupported current TimescaleDB multi-node advice.
db-replication-q1: Fixed time windows do not guarantee read-your-writes.
db-replication-q2: Clarified sync durability, quorum terminology, failover conditions and overlapping timing.
db-replication-q4: Removed unverified historical attribution and universal replication execution-order claim.
db-replication-q5: Lease self-demotion alone cannot guarantee safety under process pauses.
db-replication-q10: Four-of-six excludes two slow responses; storage quorum arithmetic is not every SQL read path.
db-replication-q11: hot_standby_feedback addresses cleanup conflicts, not all recovery cancellation.
db-replication-q12: Logical replication supports a migration strategy but does not guarantee seconds of downtime or copy all objects.
db-nosql-families-q2: Typical count is not a hard bound and comment count alone does not establish document bytes.
db-nosql-families-q3: Index absence must be explicit; duplicated query tables require reliable update propagation.
db-nosql-families-q6: Chronological lexical ordering needs normalized timestamps; GSI consistency/pagination and limits were omitted.
db-nosql-families-q7: Removed unsourced blanket comparative planner/performance and migration-cost claims.
db-nosql-families-q9: Growing-array updates do not universally resend whole documents; size estimates omit BSON overhead.
db-nosql-families-q10: Three-year retention is bounded; partition-size rules of thumb are not hard guarantees.
db-nosql-families-q11: Elasticsearch refresh defaults differ across deployments.
db-nosql-families-q12: Process termination differs from host power loss; acceptable data loss is a requirement, not universal.
db-indexing-q6: Removed one-I/O-per-insert and universal LSM performance claims.
db-indexing-q9: InnoDB covering column sets do not eliminate all MVCC clustered-record visits.
db-indexing-q10: Partial-index cleanup and visibility require more than a fixed ten-entry cost guarantee.
db-storage-internals-q3: Bloom-positive does not necessarily force a physical data-block read.
db-storage-internals-q10: Checkpoint intervals do not determine exact page-flush or recovery counts.
db-storage-internals-q12: Column layout does not imply one file or disk I/O per column; compression ratio is data-dependent.
db-relational-acid-q3: ORM defaults vary; round-trip ratio is not total endpoint speedup.
db-relational-acid-q4: Durability is configuration-dependent; FKs permit NULL and aborted physical records may remain.
db-relational-acid-q6: Hash memory fit and physical I/O cannot be inferred from row count/tree depth alone.
db-relational-acid-q9: Grouping by email only identifies users if unique and non-null.
db-relational-acid-q12: Removed unsupported universal PostgreSQL throughput claim.
db-partitioning-q2: Fraction of reassigned keys is not necessarily fraction of requests.
db-partitioning-q5: Default GetItem is eventual; explicit consistent read needed.
db-partitioning-q8: Strong per-item Query reads are not a transaction-wide snapshot over all pages.
db-transactions-isolation-q1: Fresh-snapshot behavior scoped to PostgreSQL; removed claim only Serializable considers conflicts.
db-transactions-isolation-q2: PostgreSQL Read Uncommitted does not add dirty reads; RR fix is engine-specific.
db-transactions-isolation-q3: Plain SELECT takes table locks, though not row locks.
db-transactions-isolation-q10: Read Only is a transaction mode and explicit locking queries require qualification.
db-transactions-isolation-q12: Own writes can alter later reads despite a fixed snapshot.

retrofit: db-storage-internals level-size formula: 256 MB × 10² = 25,600 MB was rounded to '≈ 25 GB' → now '= 25.6 GB' (GB defined as 1,000 MB in the block).
retrofit: db-partitioning consistent-hashing 'In words' claimed 1/N is 'the minimum any scheme can move' → now 'the minimum any scheme that keeps every node an equal share can move'.

retrofit: db-indexing lesson and questions wrote bare 'HOT', which links to module 03's Memcached HOT/WARM/COLD entry → reworded to 'HOT update' everywhere; hot-update gained aliases 'heap-only tuples', 'heap-only tuple update(s)'.
retrofit: db-partitioning-q2 worked example had doubled parentheses '(20%) (just the new node's share)' → reworded.
retrofit: glossary page-split said random keys 'leave pages about half empty' → pages are roughly half full only right after a split; now 'leave many pages only partly full'.
retrofit: glossary opensearch said 'led by AWS and now under the Linux Foundation' → forked by AWS in 2021, governed since September 2024 by the OpenSearch Software Foundation (Linux Foundation).
retrofit: glossary ora-08177 quoted the message as 'cannot serialize access' → actual text is "can't serialize access for this transaction".
retrofit: glossary semi-sync said the replica acks once it has 'received' the transaction → MySQL docs: after the events are written to its relay log (and flushed); definition updated.
retrofit: glossary mysql-group-replication definition was mostly about Orchestrator, a different tool → rewritten to define Group Replication only.
retrofit: glossary bson attributed the 16 MiB limit to BSON itself → it is MongoDB's document limit.
retrofit: glossary couchbase '1,024 vBuckets by default' → qualified to Linux and Windows (macOS uses 64; Magma buckets may use 128).

retrofit: glossary aliases that captured a different meaning removed: 'edges', 'metric', 'publication', 'on-demand' (video on demand elsewhere), 'distributed database(s)' (not all are distributed SQL), 'Capacitor' (electronic component elsewhere), 'delta encoding' (≠ delta-of-delta), 'flash memory' (≠ P/E cycle), 'OS memory' (≠ page cache), 'recovery targets'/'recovery objectives' (also cover RPO).

retrofit: glossary database-schema definition was database-only while the alias 'schema' links app-wide (API and event schemas in later modules) → generalised to the declared structure of any data, with the relational case second.
retrofit: glossary rum-conjecture had no source → attributed to Athanassoulis et al., EDBT 2016, with source; resume-driven-development source pointed at an unrelated Fowler page → source removed.
